newsitem.title: PARAGUAY: Latins seek common ground against unilateral sanctions.
newsitem.headline: Latins seek common ground against unilateral sanctions.

text.p: Representatives of Latin American countries on Friday discussed ways to counterbalance unilateral actions adopted by the United States and the European Union that affect them economically and politically, sources said.

The 14 members of Latin America's Rio Group sought to adopt resolutions regarding the U.S. drug certification process, which this year excluded Colombia and was close to sanctioning Mexico. They also planned to discuss pressures from European nations concerning environmental policies that affect trade relations.
Their concerns also include the U.S. Helms-Burton law, which sanctions foreign investments in Cuba.

Delegates of the 14-member Rio Group gathered on Friday in the Paraguayan capital of Asuncion to iron out a draft agreement to be adopted on Saturday and on Sunday, when the ministers of foreign affairs join the meeting.
Panamanian delegate Marcel Salamin told reporters the discussions will focus on the impact of unilateral policies adopted by industrialised nations, rather than on individual concerns.
"We're leaving behind the specific issue of the Helms-Burton law to address the global subject of unilateral handling of international affairs", Salamin said after the Friday meeting.
The Rio Group brings together South American countries, Mexico, and one representative each from Central America and the 13 English-speaking Caribbean nations.
A Cuban diplomat attending the meeting on Friday said the communist-ruled island would consider joining the 14-member bloc, provided no strings were attached.
"We should be interested (in joining the Rio Group) if we can join as everyone else, with no conditions attached," Cuba's consul in Asuncion, Antonio Miguel Pardo, told reporters.
